source: Amino-BPs, which account for >99% of BPs prescribed in our study, inhibit a downstream enzyme in the same metabolic pathway, farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase (FPPS), which converts geranyl pyrophosphate to farnesyl pyrophosphate (Kavanagh et al., 2006).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this mechanism with a citation.

claim: FPPS blockade disrupts protein prenylation and interferes with cytoskeletal rearrangement, membrane ruffling and vesicular trafficking in osteoclasts, thus preventing bone resorption.
source: FPPS blockade disrupts protein prenylation and interferes with cytoskeletal rearrangement, membrane ruffling and vesicular trafficking in osteoclasts, thus preventing bone resorption (Russell, 2007).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this mechanism with a citation.

source: However, the anti-osteolytic activity of BPs per se is unlikely to account for the observed association between BP use and decreased incidence of COVID-19 and, more broadly, respiratory tract infections, because patients treated with non-BP anti-resorptive bone health medications have higher odds of respiratory infections (Sing et al., 2020 and this study).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion with a citation.

claim: Mevalonate pathway inhibition by both statins and amino-BPs results in arrested endosomal maturation in antigen-presenting cells resulting in enhanced antigen presentation, T cell activation and humoral immunity.
source: Another consequence of mevalonate pathway inhibition by both statins and amino-BPs is arrested endosomal maturation in antigen-presenting cells resulting in enhanced antigen presentation, T cell activation and humoral immunity (Xia et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this mechanism with a citation.

claim: FPPS blockade by amino-BPs causes the intracellular accumulation of isopentyl diphosphate (IPP) in myeloid leukocytes, which then stimulate Vγ9Vδ2 T cells.
source: In addition to this adjuvant-like effect, FPPS blockade by amino-BPs causes the intracellular accumulation of the enzyme's substrate, isopentyl diphosphate (IPP), in myeloid leukocytes, which then stimulate Vγ9Vδ2 T cells (Wang et al., 2011; Nada et al., 2017)
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this mechanism with citations.

claim: Vγ9Vδ2 T cells are a large population of migratory innate lymphocytes in humans that are thought to play an important role in host defense against infectious pathogens.
source: FPPS blockade by amino-BPs causes the intracellular accumulation of the enzyme's substrate, isopentyl diphosphate (IPP), in myeloid leukocytes, which then stimulate Vγ9Vδ2 T cells (Wang et al., 2011; Nada et al., 2017), a large population of migratory innate lymphocytes in humans that are thought to play an important role in host defense against infectious pathogens (Ribot et al., 2021), including SARS-CoV-16.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this with citations.

claim: Experiments in humanized mice challenged with influenza viruses have shown that amino-BP-induced expansion of Vγ9Vδ2 T cells markedly improves viral control and mitigates disease severity and mortality.
source: Experiments in humanized mice that were challenged with influenza viruses have shown that amino-BP-induced expansion of Vγ9Vδ2 T cells markedly improves viral control and mitigates disease severity and mortality (Tu et al., 2011; Zheng et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with citations.

claim: Statins act upstream of FPPS and have been shown to counteract the stimulatory effect of amino-BPs on Vγ9Vδ2 T cells.
source: However, since statins act upstream of FPPS, they are expected to inhibit IPP synthesis and, hence, have been shown to counteract the stimulatory effect of amino-BPs on Vγ9Vδ2 T cells (Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this mechanism with a citation.

source: In vitro, concomitant statin and amino-BP use has been shown to be synergistic in inhibition of cancer cell growth, but mainly through downstream inhibition of geranylgeranyl transferases and subsequent protein prenylation by statins (Abdullah et al., 2017).

source: The fact that the observed reduction in COVID-19-related outcomes in BP users was not altered by concomitant statin use implies that the apparent protective effects of amino-BPs may not rely solely on stimulation of Vγ9Vδ2 T cells.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this inference based on the findings.

source: Indeed, in mice (in which BPs are not known to stimulate γδ T cells), BPs potently boost systemic and mucosal antiviral antibody and T cell responses (Tonti et al., 2013).

source: This effect was also seen with non-nitrogenous BPs, which do not antagonize FPPS (Tonti et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with a citation.

source: Moreover, studies of patients treated with amino-BPs found impaired chemotaxis and generation of reactive oxygen species by neutrophils (Kuiper et al., 2012; Chadwick et al., 2020)

claim: BPs may provide therapeutic benefits during infections with SARS-CoV-2 through modulation of both innate and adaptive immune responses.
source: Thus, BPs may provide therapeutic benefits during infections with SARS-CoV-2 through modulation of both innate and adaptive immune responses.

claim: The association between BP use and decreased odds of COVID-19-related endpoints was robust in analyses comparing BP users to BP non-users regardless of age, sex or geographic location.
source: We conclude that, despite several caveats discussed above, the association between BP use and decreased odds of COVID-19-related endpoints was robust in analyses comparing BP users to BP non-users. evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion.

claim: BPs should be considered for prophylactic use in individuals at risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: These retrospective findings strongly suggest that BPs should be considered for prophylactic use in individuals at risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly makes this recommendation based on the findings.

source: Rare, but severe adverse events that have been linked to BP use include osteonecrosis of the jaw (Migliorati et al., 2006) and atypical femur fractures (Saita et al., 2015), which are both associated with long-term BP therapy.

source: Remarkably, BP users of alendronic acid whose prescription ended more than eight months prior to the observation period, as well as users who initiated alendronic acid therapy immediately preceding the observation period, had similarly decreased odds of COVID-19-related outcomes (Figure 3B).
